name: Fertiliser supply
value: Gulf urea route disrupted, not shut
summary: Gulf fertiliser exports still exposed to Hormuz attacks; route not closed, so Alert unconfirmed
state: Hormuz carries a large share of world urea exports, and US and Iranian forces clashed near the strait as a response to a proposed deal was awaited (gCaptain). Searches on 7 Nov found no report that the export route is closed or of urea prices up 60% in three months; analysts expect prices to stay elevated (Pro Farmer). Watch holds; the Alert is unconfirmed.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for the next season face higher, more volatile prices.
rubric_hit: Key route disrupted but not closed = Watch

sources.title: gCaptain — US, Iran clash near Hormuz as response on proposed deal awaited
Pro Farmer — Fertilizer prices have further to rise

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
